# Synapse 2.0.14

Workflows can add to a Vault file from their first run, Synapse AI sees the Vault's write wherever your setup offers it, and errors no longer show your computer's folders.

## Fixed

- **Adding a line to a Vault file works from the first run.** A workflow asked to add a line to a file in the Vault, such as a log, stopped on its first run because the file did not exist yet. Writing to the Vault can now add to the end of a file and creates the file when it is not there, and Synapse AI builds workflows that way. Two runs adding to the same file at the same moment both keep their lines.
- **Synapse AI no longer says it cannot save to the Vault when your setup can.** Where saving to the Vault is a tool an agent holds only by name, Synapse AI could not see it, so a plan to save a file or draw a chart said there was no way. It now plans with it, and a step that saves through an agent asks for that agent to have the tool by name.
- **Errors and run results no longer show your computer's folders.** A Vault file is named by its place in the Vault, such as `reports/sales.csv`, in the Vault tools' answers and in a failed step's message, and your home folder shows as `~`. Workflows saved with the old full paths still work.
- **Patching a Vault file with nothing to find is refused** instead of putting the new text at the top of the file.

## Install

**macOS and Linux**

```bash
curl -LsSf https://synapseorch.com/install.sh | bash
```

**Windows (PowerShell)**

```powershell
irm https://synapseorch.com/install.ps1 | iex
```

<details>
<summary>npm, pip or Docker</summary>

```bash
npm install -g synapse-orch-ai && synapse
pip install synapse-orch-ai && synapse         # Python 3.11–3.14 and Node.js 20.9+
```

For Docker, see [Docker](https://docs.synapseorch.com/getting-started/docker): the image is `synapseorchai/synapse-ai:2.0.14`, also `:latest`.
</details>

## Upgrading

- **From 2.0.x:** run `synapse upgrade`. Your data stays where it is, and the database is backed up first.
- **From 1.x:** run `synapse upgrade` on your 1.x install. It moves you to 2.0 the same way 2.0.0 did; read the [2.0.0 notes](https://github.com/synapseorch-ai/synapse-ai/releases/tag/v2.0.0) for what changes.

**Full changelog:** [v2.0.13...v2.0.14](https://github.com/synapseorch-ai/synapse-ai/compare/v2.0.13...v2.0.14) · [Documentation](https://docs.synapseorch.com)
